alt: Buckled concrete slabs with rebar pushed upward across northbound lanes of Interstate 97 in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, after extreme July 4th heat caused the pavement to blow out
story: On July 4th, 2026, record heat caused a concrete section of I-97 near Baltimore to buckle and thrust broken slabs and exposed rebar upward across all three northbound lanes; engineers note the road was designed to historical temperature specs that assumed modern July heat would never occur.
why_funny: American infrastructure failed spectacularly on Independence Day because mid-20th century engineers built roads for a climate that no longer exists — and the fix takes six to nine hours on a holiday weekend.
